entry.title: Palomar - a registry of Lean-verified mathematics

link.title: Palomar - a registry of Lean-verified mathematics

entry.content:
Palomar, a new public registry of machine-checked mathematical results formalized in Lean, launched in August 2026. Initially incubated by Lean FRO and ICARM, Palomar provides a searchable and durable record of formalizations, including the exact statements checked,

Matthew Ballard serves as one of Palomar’s four initial Technical Maintainers and as an initial Moderator and member of its Scientific Advisory Board. More details are on the about page.

entry.title: AI for Mathematics panel at ICM 2026

link.title: AI for Mathematics panel at ICM 2026

entry.content:
Matthew Ballard participated in the AI for Mathematics panel at the 2026 International Congress of Mathematicians in Philadelphia. Moderated by Emily Riehl, the panel also included Bogdan Georgiev, Javier Gómez-Serrano, Terence Tao, and Geordie Williamson.

The discussion focused on the impact of AI on mathematical research practice, including theorem proving, writing and refereeing, the development of junior researchers, and how the mathematical community can use new technology while advancing human understanding of mathematics.

entry.title: Mathematics in Lean at ICMS 2026
entry.content:
Together with Rémy Degenne and Damiano Testa, Matthew Ballard co-organized the Mathematics in Lean session at the International Congress on Mathematical Software 2026. The session brought together research in mathematical formalization using Lean with new tools and software for formal mathematics, including work on AI-assisted formalization and the formalization of current mathematical research.

Ballard was also a coauthor of the ICMS proceedings paper “A Macaulay2-Lean interface for proofs in Lean” with Anton Leykin, Michael E. Stillman, Damiano Testa, Douglas A. Torrance, and Jay Yang, work arising from the Bridging Proof and Computation project.

entry.title: National Academies meeting on organizing mathematical knowledge

link.title: National Academies meeting on organizing mathematical knowledge

entry.content:
Matthew Ballard participated in the National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine meeting Organizing Mathematical Knowledge in the Age of AI and Formalization in Washington, D.C. The two-day meeting examined how formalization and AI are changing the creation, organization, verification, and use of mathematical knowledge.

Ballard served on the opening Panel on the Current Landscape and Challenges in Formalization and AI, moderated by Melanie Matchett Wood, together with Javier Gómez-Serrano, Jesse Han, Jaume de Dios Pont, and Jason Reed. The event page has more information.

entry.title: Mathlib awarded the 2026 Jean-Pierre Demailly Prize

link.title: Mathlib awarded the 2026 Jean-Pierre Demailly Prize

entry.content:
Mathlib, the collaborative library of formalized mathematics in Lean for which Matthew Ballard serves as a maintainer, was awarded the 2026 Jean-Pierre Demailly Prize for Open Science in Mathematics. The international biennial prize recognizes projects contributing to open science through scientific publishing, mathematical collaboration, or free mathematical software.

The jury highlighted Mathlib’s broad significance for the future of mathematics, its central role in formalization and verification, and its open and collaborative model for creating, checking, preserving, and reusing mathematical knowledge at scale.

entry.title: AI for Math - Bridging proof and computation

link.title: AI for Math - Bridging proof and computation

entry.content:
As part of a collaboration with Anton Leykin, Mike Stillman, and Damiano Testa, Matthew Ballard has been awarded an AI for Math grant for the project “Bridging proof and computation”.

The project focuses on developing an extensible, native interface between Lean and the computational algebra system (CAS) Macaulay2 (M2) to enhance the integration between CAS and formal proof verification. By creating a Lean-based domain-specific language (DSL) for interacting with M2, the team aims to enable seamless bidirectional communication, allowing Lean users to call M2 functions and M2 users to generate Lean proofs. This initiative will also look to formalizes key algorithms in M2 and explores the development a general computer algebra system (CAS) interface for Lean, potentially benefiting other CAS systems in the future.

entry.title: Institute for Computer-Aided Reasoning in Mathematics (ICARM)

link.title: Institute for Computer-Aided Reasoning in Mathematics (ICARM)

entry.content: Matthew Ballard is the founding Associate Director for Scientific Activities at the Institute for Computer-Aided Reasoning in Mathematics, ICARM, a new NSF- and Simons Foundation-funded national mathematics institute designed to accelerate mathematical research and empower mathematicians through all faces of AI, including formal methods, automated reasoning, and machine learning. ICARM will employ a dedicated staff of Innovation Engineers to work with researchers to develop and deploy new tools and techniques for computer-aided reasoning in mathematics. The institute operates on a three-year pilot, also hosting summer schools, workshops, small research groups, and conferences to foster interdisciplinary collaboration.

entry.title: FRG on multigraded commutative algebra, toric varieties, and mirror symmetry

link.title: FRG on multigraded commutative algebra, toric varieties, and mirror symmetry

entry.content: As part of an NSF Focused Research Group (FRG) with Christine Berkesch, Michael K. Brown, Daniel Erman, David Favero, Sheel Ganatra, and Andrew Hanlon, Matthew Ballard has been awarded a grant for the project “Multigraded Commutative Algebra, Toric Varieties, and Homological Mirror Symmetry.” This collaboration will unite expertise in commutative algebra, algebraic geometry, and symplectic geometry to develop new tools, solve longstanding problems, and build connections between these fields. The FRG will also provide training and mentoring opportunities through workshops, seminars, and open computational resources.

entry.content: Matthew Ballard joined the Strategic Advisory Board of the Mathlib Initiative, an organization supporting the continued development and long-term sustainability of Mathlib. He continues to serve as a Mathlib maintainer.

entry.title: Fellow of the American Mathematical Society

link.title: Fellow of the American Mathematical Society

entry.content:
It is a deep honor to be named a Fellow of the American Mathematical Society.

The AMS Fellows program recognizes members who have made outstanding contributions to the creation, exposition, advancement, communication, and utilization of mathematics.

It is a long journey from finishing second in a high school calculus contest. Along the way I have benefited from my many mentors, colleagues, and students. Immense gratitude goes to them and to my family for their unwavering support.

I am grateful to the AMS for this recognition. I look forward to contributing meaningfully to the mission of mathematics in the years to come.
entry.summary: It is a deep honor to be named a Fellow of the American Mathematical Society.
